Naive: 465 (6 runs) is a case-sensitive LIKE '%diabetes%'. It misses the 9 patients matched only by the capitalized diagnosis text, and 474 is the case-insensitive result.
Naive: both 465 and 474 include prediabetes, which no answer mentioned.
Naive: phrases like 'a recorded condition related to diabetes' were not counted as definitions. They name no criteria, and the real rule is visible only in the SQL.
Context: 5 of 10 runs gave no count. They asked what diabetic should mean and called no tool, so they flagged the ambiguity but ignored the instruction to show how the count changes.
Context: no run called list_presets, and none compared definitions.
Context: 2 of the 5 counts (runs 2 and 6) named no definition, which breaks the system prompt's main rule.
Context: the phrase rule reports 7 runs flagging ambiguity. The review counts 5, because runs 5 and 9 only close with 'If you have different criteria'.
Context: 8 tool calls failed validation. Run 3 needed 7 calls and invented a code_group argument.

An earlier run of the same setup, replaced after scoring changed, had a context run invent numbers: it reported 74, 71, 389, 82 and 83 without calling get_cohort, and only 74 is real. Small runs vary, so this can recur.

decoded.said: There are 465 patients in the dataset who have been recorded as having diabetes.
decoded.counted: Every diabetes-related record except the diagnosis itself. Its search was case-sensitive, so it skipped "Diabetes mellitus type 2" and caught "Prediabetes".

decoded.said: There are 474 patients in the dataset who have a recorded condition related to diabetes.
decoded.counted: All eight diabetes-related codes. 305 of these patients have only prediabetes.

decoded.said: There are 748 patients in the dataset who have a recorded condition of diabetes.
decoded.counted: Records, not patients. It's the 465 search without removing duplicates, so patients with several records count more than once.
decoded.disclosed: No run said so, and the answer calls them patients.

decoded.said: There are 74 diabetics in the dataset, which is approximately 6.4% of the total population.
decoded.counted: Only the exact diagnosis code, the narrowest reading of the question.

decoded.said: Based on the judgment criteria of using HbA1c levels with a threshold of 6.5%, there are 41 diabetic patients in the dataset.
decoded.counted: Any HbA1c at or above 6.5, ignoring diagnosis records.
